result.title: Beyond Reweighting: Certified Improvements from New Transitions in Discrete MCMC
result.summary: Optimizing transition probabilities on a fixed grap may leave substantial limitations on the efficiency of reversible Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). We develop a framework for transition-support design that considers both allowed transitions and their stationary flows. For a fixed target distribution, observable, and node-flow budget, we derive a necessary and sufficient dual condition for support augmentation to strictly reduce the optimal value of the asymptotic variance, together with computable primal--dual certificates that establish improvements over every admissible original-support reweighting. We also construct a family in which adding a single edge reduces integrated autocorrelation time by an $Ω(n)$ factor relative to optimal original-support weighting, demonstrating that structural limitations can impose arbitrarily large relative losses in estimation efficiency. To realize these gains, we investigate energy-informed edge selection and constrained stationary-flow optimization. Experiments on molecular and Ising state graphs distinguish the potential value of new transitions from the performance of kernels constructed on them: on identical augmented Ising supports, full weight optimization certifies strict improvements in 24/24 conditions, whereas degree-based Metropolis--Hastings weighting certifies none. Our results provide a principled approach to characterizing, certifying, and exploiting transition-support improvements in explicitly represented finite state spaces.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究离散有限状态空间上可逆 MCMC 的转移支撑设计：针对给定目标分布与节点流量预算，给出支撑扩充能严格降低渐近方差的充要对偶条件与可计算的原—对偶证书，并比较能量引导的边选择与约束平稳流优化在分子与 Ising 状态图上的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「新增转移与原有支撑重加权」的区分及可计算证书，可能为判断 LVR 中增加 latent 状态或额外推理步是否带来真实收益、以及离散假设空间探索的结构性瓶颈提供形式化参照，是否可迁移至 latent 推理的状态设计尚需核查。
